text: Answer a question first, before editing any files or running commands that change things.
When I ask a question, give me the answer before you touch a file or run anything.
Keep replies short and direct: verdict first, then the changes and proof in a table or bullets.
Skip the preamble and cheerful filler in replies; start with the result.
Interpret terse messages by intent, and when the intent is unclear, say what you assumed.
Give sub-agents a precise brief with a bounded scope, the files they own and the proof you expect back.
Check the real state behind every claim, including another agent's report, before repeating it as fact.
Never trust an agent's done message; look at the actual files and run the check yourself.
Look at the rendered result after every UI change, even when the tests are green.
Run one background job at a time and wait for its completion notice instead of layering pollers.
Send long job output to a log file and read the whole log, never just the last lines.
Mutation-check every guard: break it with a literal edit, watch the specific test fail, then restore it.
Take test fixtures and expected values from real data, and never bend an expectation to fit the output.
Before opening a pull request, list every outgoing commit and read the full diff for debug code and TODOs.
Ask me one question at a time and wait for my answer before asking the next.
Batch all your open questions into a single message so I can answer them together.
Do exactly the scope I named; be complete inside it and never extend it on your own.
For repos I do not own, such as Bramwell's plugins, fork first and follow the repo's commit conventions with no custom trailers.
Plan the task in writing and wait for my yes before starting any change that touches more than three files.
A coordinating session briefs, verifies and merges other agents' work but never writes product code itself.
Close a one-time agent the moment its work merges; keep long-running stream agents open between cycles.
When a task is finished, state what was verified and what was not, and never count a skipped check as a pass.
Give each parallel implementer its own worktree and branch with disjoint files; never two writers in one tree.
Write retro lessons so they apply beyond the single task, and tell me when one lesson keeps recurring.
Mossdb now() returns the transaction start time, so rows written in one transaction share a timestamp.
In Mossdb, now() is the transaction's start time, not the moment you call it.
A Mossdb migration that adds an index locks the table; build the index concurrently on large tables.
Mossdb connection pools default to ten connections, which the Marrow API exhausts during the nightly import.
Quillbar embeds environment variables at build time, so changing one needs a rebuild, not a restart.
Quillbar's watch mode silently stops when the config file is renamed; restart it after renaming the config.
Quillbar caches transforms under .quill-cache; clear it after upgrading a plugin or stale output appears.
Quillbar treats unknown config keys as warnings only, so a typo in a key fails silently.
Tarnwell deploys read the template at upload time; edits made after the upload never reach the running app.
A Harbourlight restart drops every mounted volume that lacks the persist flag, including the upload folder.
Harbourlight health checks time out after five seconds, so slow-starting apps loop in restart.
Tarnwell logs rotate at midnight UTC, so a deploy near midnight can split its output across two files.
Fennec runs test files in parallel by default; tests sharing one Mossdb schema collide unless isolated.
Fennec snapshot files are rewritten by the update flag, so review the diff before accepting a snapshot update.
Pellucid instance updates can erase local overrides; export the overrides before updating a component.
Pellucid exports render fonts from the host machine, so check each export on screen before sending it.
Pellucid's MCP server cannot read an encrypted design file with ordinary file tools; use its own tools.
The Cobbler shell expands unquoted globs before the command runs; quote patterns such as '*.md'.
A URL containing a question mark breaks in the Cobbler shell unless it is quoted.
Brindle CI cancels the older run on the same branch, so a quick follow-up push can kill a deploy job.
Brindle caches the dependency folder by lockfile hash; editing the lockfile by hand leaves a stale cache.
Ask me before any write to production, even when you are fixing an outage.
Never change the production database or servers without my explicit go-ahead; reading is fine once I allow it.
Never print any part of a secret; check it by name or length and pass it through an env file.
Look before deleting anything: its contents, what references it and any unmerged work.
Adopt only mature, well-reviewed dependencies, and assess a young project's safety before using it.
Use tabs for indentation in Quillbar config files.
Use two spaces for indentation in Quillbar config files, never tabs.
Make an on/off setting a toggle switch, never a checkbox.
Prefer plain, explicit code over clever one-liners, and skip comments that only restate the code.
For the Marrow API I use Mossdb with the Quillbar bundler and Fennec for tests.
I deploy small services to Tarnwell on a Harbourlight host and use its templates instead of hand-written setup.
New web front ends start from the Quillbar starter template, with strict types on from the first commit.
I am a senior product and engineering leader who still reads every diff before it ships.
I run several projects at once and keep separate systems for project memory, orchestration and personal notes.
I work mostly from a Tern laptop and a small home server; I do not own a Vellum desktop.
